# Vidsc Flyleaf source integration

Current status (14 October 2026): the read-only presentation sub-gate is accepted; full M1 remains
OPEN for real-media B1–B6 and bounded visual/manual acceptance. See
[presentation acceptance](../../docs/validation/2026-10-14-m1-presentation-acceptance.md): **241/241**
unit tests, **140/140** final five-fixture visible checks, **19/19** final visible lifecycle checks
plus lifecycle actions, and **108/108** earlier exhaustive VFR adjacency checks. This session stops
after M1 and its tests; interval editing/export are not implemented.
The default Release verification passes source/native manifests, CLI/barcodes, packaged scene
windows, application smoke and promotion (`artifacts/m1-qualified-release-build.log`); B6 clean-location
`Test-Delivery` remains unrun.

Upstream: https://github.com/SuRGeoNix/Flyleaf, exact commit `0f061769c47d50dfdae5c667435bf6548a0dc121` (the repository commit recorded in FlyleafLib 3.11.11 NuGet metadata). Imported with `git archive` limited to FlyleafLib, LICENSE.txt and its package icon; upstream applications and history excluded. Upstream project declares 3.11.10 despite the published 3.11.11 package recording this commit.

License: LGPL-3.0-or-later; original LICENSE.txt and all source notices retained. Ship the license and corresponding modified source with redistributions according to its terms.

The local project targets net10.0-windows, Version 3.11.11, informational version `3.11.11+vidsc.hook.1`. All upstream dependency versions remain exact, including Flyleaf.FFmpeg.Bindings 9.0.2 and Vortice 3.8.3. Empty local props isolate upstream nullable/compiler and package version policy from the application. Native playback libraries remain the separately pinned playback ABI set; CLI FFmpeg is not interchangeable.

Changes cover scalar raw decoded-frame metadata, typed presentation evidence, source/decode/operation epochs, scheduling token capture, render/backbuffer submission association, edit-list preroll seeking and raw-HRESULT DXGI confirmation with a bounded 256-entry map and independent polling. A non-overlapping confirmation timer uses `DwmFlush` only for pending evidence and outside renderer locks; failure cannot certify a frame. Notifications are immutable and delivered asynchronously on a single owned worker, outside native/renderer locks. No GPU surface is retained by the tracker. The public entry point is `Player.Presentation`; declaration and callback contracts are in `MediaFramework/MediaRenderer/PresentationTracker.cs`.

Native events supply evidence, not a global trust switch. The Vidsc adapter qualifies the pinned hook as `Proven` through its read-only `IObservedPresentationSource` getter. Each read checks current source, operation, swap-chain epoch and confirmed present ID; normalized start/end additionally require settled submission and a matching complete source map. Missing map/end returns null; EOF requires independent terminal verification. Native `NextRawPts` remains unknown rather than deriving an end from nominal FPS or raw duration. Core stores no second native observation. Missing source PTS or exact container epoch is preserved as null. PTS and best-effort are captured before Flyleaf normalization, on all three receive paths. Decoder setup activates staged source generation; seek requests and step render scheduling retain their specific operation context. Decoder work with a stale token is rejected. A fresh seek or explicit Pause→Play scheduling barrier can re-arm the current presentation intent; callbacks never retag already scheduled work. Native present-ID baselines survive application operation changes and ResizeBuffers, while a recreated native swapchain starts a new count epoch.

Build: `dotnet build third_party/FlyleafLib/FlyleafLib/FlyleafLib.csproj -c Release -m:1 --disable-build-servers`. Application project references use this source tree. The native prerequisite experiment and original hook decision remain historical evidence; current qualification is recorded in the presentation acceptance document linked above. Interval editing and production export remain disabled because those later features are unimplemented.

Modified upstream files: FlyleafLib.csproj; MediaFramework/MediaDecoder/VideoDecoder.cs; MediaFramework/MediaFrame/VideoFrame.cs; MediaFramework/MediaRenderer/Renderer.Device.cs, Renderer.Present.cs and SwapChain.cs; MediaPlayer/Player.cs, Player.Playback.cs, Player.Extra.cs, Player.Screamers.cs and Player.Screamers.VASD.cs. Added PresentationTracker.cs and Properties/VidscTests.cs (test access only). Configuration and license/icon files are tracked alongside the source. Build outputs are ignored. The pristine source archive SHA256 is recorded in the diagnostic vendor-foundation/build-identity.json; production build identity is generated from tracked source hashes by the release workflow.

Historical foundation validation: isolated vendor compiles; standalone production-source probe runs actual playback and a final paused seek and confirms the latter through independent polling without another Present (`artifacts/experiments/m1-hook/production-native.jsonl`, exit 0). Focused actual-tracker regressions cover operation baseline, uint wrap, disjoint after confirmation, swapchain reset/resize, source replacement and final paused timeout. These early checks alone did not prove presentation end or exact edit eligibility. The final application/visible qualification and independently checked source-map ends are recorded in the current presentation acceptance document; failed intermediate runs remain in the source-hook validation history.

Paused recovery API: `Player.TryRefreshPresentation(intent)` schedules a fresh render of the owned cached same-source frame only after native seek/play ownership is drained. It preserves original raw metadata, validates the frozen current operation and reports scheduling only. `PresentationSeekIdle` is an asynchronous advisory wakeup after seek cleanup, enabling a pending recovery attempt without polling or sleeping. It is never presentation evidence. Reset/resize clears the old backbuffer identity before any subsequent native submit.
